raidVictorySlides.text: The battle is won! Finn lies defeated, his reign of terror ended. Rodrick claps you on the shoulder. 'Not bad, kid. Not bad at all.'
Back at the barracks, Matthias offers you a seat. 'You've got the makings of a Tidehunter,' he says. 'We could use someone like you. Think about it.'
This branch ends here in the current version. Driftwatch goes on, and so can you.

lukePrologueSlides.text: The story of Luke begins, as many in the Whispers do, with the sea's cruel embrace. His mother, Elara, succumbed to childbirth's fevered grip, and his father, a fisherman named Gareth, was claimed by a sudden squall that showed no mercy. Orphaned before he could even speak his name, he was brought to Leo's Lighthouse, a beacon of hope standing defiant against the salt-sprayed cliffs of Driftwatch. Here, under the watchful eye of the kindly Old Leo, his life truly began.

In the orphanage's quiet halls, he forged a family not of blood, but of bond. There was Sarah, whose sweet nature made her the steadfast 'mother' of their small group; Robert, the strong, serious boy who dreamed of a life beyond the docks; and young Kyle, whose mischievous grin was a constant source of trouble and laughter. Surrounded by his only friends, Luke's tragic past became a foundation, not an anchor. His sharp mind, a gift from a life of observation, became his tool—a beacon of potential promising a future far grander than his humble beginnings.

wakeupEventSlides.text: You wake in a cramped room at the Salty Mug. Old Man Finn bangs on the door: ‘Two months without rent, kid. Out.’ The lesson ends. The day begins.
Kicked to the streets, you step into Driftwatch’s slums. The real world doesn’t wait—and neither should you.

finnDebtIntroSlides.text: You wake to Old Man Finn staring down, a guard idling beside him—knife glinting.

breakfastEventSlides.text: You share a simple breakfast at Leo’s Lighthouse—warm bread, salted fish, and a quiet moment before the day.

playEventSlidesSarah.text: You spend time with Sarah, helping tidy the common room and laughing at quiet memories. Her calm steadies you more than you'd admit.

playEventSlidesRobert.text: You trade jabs with Robert and talk dreams bigger than the docks. Work hard, aim higher, and don't let the wind decide your path.

playEventSlidesKyle.text: You chase Kyle through the lighthouse halls, laughing as he slips past your reach. Mischief fades, leaving the night a little lighter.

playEventSlidesAlone.text: You spend a quiet hour by yourself. The lighthouse hums with distant voices, but your thoughts are your own—clear, steady, and sharp.

smugglerTrapSlides.text: A frantic knock jolts you awake. Kyle whispers through the door: ‘Luke, get up—Robert’s slipped out. Something’s wrong.’
You and Kyle hurry to the docks. Lanterns sway in the wind; shadows move between stacked crates.
Down by the water, Robert meets figures in the dark. You stay low—watching, listening—ready to act.

robertCaughtSlides.text: The smugglers overwhelm Robert, blades flashing in the dark. He takes blow after blow, but refuses to fall. With a desperate shout, he throws himself at the attackers. 'Run! Get Kyle out of here!' he screams, sacrificing himself. You grab Kyle and sprint into the night, the sounds of the struggle fading behind you.
Back in the safety of the lighthouse, you and Kyle collapse, gasping for air. The silence is heavy, broken only by Kyle's quiet sobs. Robert is gone.

gameOverSlides.text: Luke has fallen in battle. His journey ends here.

starvationSlides.text: Hunger gnaws at your insides until there is nothing left. You collapse, too weak to rise again. Your journey ends in silence.

timeoutSlides.text: The debt has aged past seven days. The moment you step back into Driftwatch proper, Finn's people close in and drag you into the reckoning he promised.

rebelRaidIntroSlides.text: You gather with Rodrick, Matthias, and Stan at the Tidehunter Quarter. 'Suit up, kid,' Rodrick grunts, tossing you a bundle of iron gear. 'You'll need this where we're going.' You equip the heavy iron armor and grip the sword, feeling the weight of the coming battle.
The four of you approach the Salty Mug under the cover of darkness. The tavern's lights spill out onto the street, but inside, trouble is brewing. Matthias signals the advance. It's time to end this.
You burst through the doors! Finn stands up, knocking over his chair. 'You?! And the Guard?!' He sneers, snapping his fingers. Three thugs step out from the shadows. 'Kill them all!'

You gather with Rodrick, Matthias, and Stan at the Tidehunter Quarter. 'Suit up, kid,' Rodrick grunts, tossing you a bundle of iron gear. 'You'll need this where we're going.' You equip the heavy iron armor and grip the sword, feeling the weight of the coming battle.
The squad moves in on the Salty Mug. Customers scatter as you siege the tavern, clearing the main floor. The path to Finn is open.
You corner Finn in the back room! He sneers, snapping his fingers. 'You?! And the Guard?! Kill them all!' Three thugs step out from the shadows.

rebelVictorySlides.text: Finn falls, his grip over the slums broken. Rodrick nods once. 'You've got guts, kid. Maybe the Guard could use someone like you.' This branch ends here in the current version, but Driftwatch is still yours to walk.

elaraDeliverySlides.text: You navigate the twisting alleys of the slums until you find the recipient—a twitchy man in the shadows. He grabs the package, checks the contents, and nods. The 'medicine' has been delivered.

berylDeliverySlides.text: You wait at the servant's entrance of a grand estate until a noblewoman arrives. She takes the parcel with a cool glance and signs the receipt with a practiced hand. The delivery is complete.

benCheatEventSlides.text: The cards fly. Ben sweats. You signal from the side—a cough, a tap. He catches on. Slowly, the pile of silvers in front of him grows. He cashes out before they catch on.

sellLocketSlides.text: You present the antique locket to the noble collector. He studies it for a long moment, then counts out ten silver coins into your hand without hesitation. 'A fair price for such history,' he says, pocketing the locket. The debt payment is secured.

evilEndingSlides.text: You take the key and head deep into the slums, finding the hidden grate Finn mentioned. The air is thick with rot as you descend into the darkness.
Deep in the tunnels, you find a strange, sealed door. The charm pulses with a faint light. You place it in the recess, and the stone grinds open...
This branch ends here in the current version. You can keep playing and see what else Driftwatch is willing to show you.

hybridEndingSlides.text: You step out of the Salty Mug with thirty silvers lighter in your pouch and Finn's words heavier in your head. You were hard when you had to be, soft when you chose to be, and Driftwatch is still standing either way.

The slums swallow you back up. Debtors, guards, smugglers, saints in rags – none of them know what kind of man you are yet. Maybe you don't either. But for now, you're alive, and the city is wide open.
This branch ends here in the current version. You can keep playing from here.

whitefangFinnKillSlides.text: White Fang answers before Finn can. The tavern seems to dim around the glaive as Luke steps in and ends the old debt collector with a violence too swift to bargain with.
Finn is gone. Whatever fear held the Salty Mug together dies with him, and the people who watched know instinctively that something worse now walks away from the room.
This branch ends here in the current version. White Fang remains with you, and Driftwatch is still open.

finnPersonalKillSlides.text: Finn dies by Luke's hand, not the Guard's. No warrant, no raid, no borrowed authority - only the kind of ending Driftwatch understands best.
With Finn gone, the debt that dragged you through the city is broken at the source. Whatever comes next in Driftwatch, it will not be under his shadow.
This branch ends here in the current version. You can keep playing from here.

whitefangUnreadableWoodsSlides.text: Strange storm-marked letters drift in the air between the trees, fading whenever you try to focus on them. Luke reaches toward them, but the meaning slips away before thought can catch it.

whitefangUnreadableBeachSlides.text: Along the lonely shore, pale signs flicker above the sand like writing made from salt and lightning. Luke feels something in them, but whatever language they carry remains closed to him.

whitefangUnreadableMountainSlides.text: High on the stony path, the same storm letters turn in the cold air. Luke can feel intent in them, almost memory, but he still cannot comprehend what this energy means.

whitefangWoodsVisionSlides.text: When Luke touches the storm letters with Shihan's translation still fresh in his mind, the woods change around him. He sees Ren Zhen younger than the legends, White Fang across his back, studying broken branches and blackened roots where corruption once passed.
The vision carries no words, only certainty: Ren Zhen hunted with patience here, learning the mage's trail instead of rushing toward glory. Every sign in the undergrowth mattered.

whitefangBeachVisionSlides.text: At the isolated shore, the sea wind becomes another age. Ren Zhen stands against storm and surf with White Fang in both hands, the long pursuit finally brought to its end.

The mage dies here amid black surf, broken ritual, and lightning. What Luke feels in the vision is not triumph, but finality. The hunt that stole six years of Ren Zhen's life ended on this beach, and Driftwatch kept the memory long after Shenhai lost the trail.

whitefangMountainVisionSlides.text: The final storm letters open into thin mountain air and old exhaustion. Ren Zhen climbs alone, White Fang heavy in his hands, age finally visible in every step.

He reaches a hidden cave and seals himself beyond stone and silence. The last thing Luke feels from the vision is not triumph, but restraint: an old warrior choosing where the weapon's darkness would be buried when his own heart could no longer hold it.

whitefangCaveBlockedSlides.text: You find the hidden fault in the mountain exactly where the vision led you. Great slabs of stone have been collapsed inward with deliberate force. Whatever Ren Zhen sealed here, he meant to deny to the world.
You can go no farther alone. The passage would need tools, powder, and hands trained not to flinch in tight stone.

whitefangExpeditionBreachSlides.text: You return to the hidden mountain fault with Shihan Yue, Captain Lin Shao, Wei Taren, and Qiao Ren. The place from the vision is real. Cold wind cuts along the stone while the four of them study the sealed cave Ren Zhen chose for his final disappearance.

At Shihan's word, the retainers unpack lacquered Shenhai charges wrapped against the damp. They set them into the old fracture lines with practiced precision while Shihan watches the seam in silence, as if she already knows something inside is listening.

The blast rolls through the heights like a buried storm. Stone splits, darkness opens, and a figure steps from the cave with White Fang in hand. What waits within is not Ren Zhen as he lived, but the shadow that remained behind to guard the glaive.

whitefangBindingSlides.text: Ren Zhen's shadow falls, and what remains of the old Guardian finally breaks apart. Yet White Fang of Heaven does not lie still. Lightning crawls across the glaive as if searching for a heart still strong enough to endure it.

The weapon chooses Luke. Storm-light tears through bone, memory, and breath as the last of Ren Zhen's ruined will pours out of flesh and into steel. What remains human in him is gone. What remains in you is harder, colder, and far less merciful.

When it ends, White Fang of Heaven rests in your hands as if it had always belonged there. The good is buried in the glaive. What walks away from the mountain is only what was strong enough to bear the rest. Ordinary people will feel the difference long before you learn how to hide it.
